cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Hey! I’m Niko. Your Vision Investigator Officer.
segments: Hey! I’m Niko. Your Vision Investigator Officer.
cues.visualCue: Niko materialises and waves; medium shot

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: So you want to know how light becomes sight?
segments: So you want to know how light becomes sight?
cues.visualCue: Niko gestures toward the starlight beam

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Then watching from out here won't help.
segments: Then watching from out here won't help.
cues.visualCue: Niko turns toward the subdued display; human figure appears after this line

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: We need to go inside somewhere humans can't.
segments: We need to go inside somewhere humans can't.
cues.visualCue: Wide: Niko and the revealed human

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Click on the SCAN button.
segments: Click on the SCAN button.
cues.visualCue: Niko raises his hand; SCAN button pulses

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: There.
segments: There.
cues.visualCue: One eye illuminates as the line starts

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Your first destination.
segments: Your first destination.
cues.visualCue: Anatomical close-up of the eye inside the skull

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Here it is. The human eye.
segments: Here it is. The human eye.
cues.visualCue: Enlarged eye in front of learner, slow rotation

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: It has several parts, and each one has an important job.
segments: It has several parts, and each one has an important job.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Click or ask Niko about each part to explore what it does.
segments: Click or ask Niko about each part to explore what it does.
cues.visualCue: After Niko's snap: sclera, cornea, iris, pupil highlight in turn

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: This tough white outer layer is called the sclera. It protects the eye and helps maintain its shape.
segments: This tough white outer layer is called the sclera.
It protects the eye and helps maintain its shape.
cues.visualCue: Close-up of sclera; other parts translucent

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: This transparent, curved layer at the front is the cornea. It protects the eye and bends incoming light.
segments: This transparent, curved layer at the front is the cornea.
It protects the eye and bends incoming light.
cues.visualCue: Close-up of cornea profile; other parts translucent

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: This coloured part is the iris. It controls the size of the pupil.
segments: This coloured part is the iris. It controls the size of the pupil.
cues.visualCue: Front close-up of iris; other parts translucent

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: This opening is the pupil. Light enters the eye through it.
segments: This opening is the pupil. Light enters the eye through it.
cues.visualCue: Pupil rim highlighted as an opening; camera pulls back

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: We’ve seen the parts we can see from the outside. Now, let’s look inside.
segments: We’ve seen the parts we can see from the outside. Now, let’s look inside.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Click on the Inside View button to see how the eye looks from the inside.
segments: Click on the Inside View button to see how the eye looks from the inside.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Click or ask Niko about each part to explore what it does.
segments: Click or ask Niko about each part to explore what it does.
cues.visualCue: Cutaway eye; internal parts highlight in turn

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: This space between the cornea and the lens contains a clear fluid called aqueous humour.
segments: This space between the cornea and the lens contains a clear fluid called aqueous humour.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: It helps nourish the front parts of the eye and helps maintain pressure inside the eye.
segments: It helps nourish the front parts of the eye and helps maintain pressure inside the eye.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Behind the pupil is the eye’s natural crystalline lens.
segments: Behind the pupil is the eye’s natural crystalline lens.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: It is transparent, flexible and biconvex, meaning it bulges outward on both sides.
segments: It is transparent, flexible and biconvex, meaning it bulges outward on both sides.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: It can change its shape to help focus light from objects at different distances.
segments: It can change its shape to help focus light from objects at different distances.
cues.visualCue: Lens changes shape slightly; view widens

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Most of the space behind the lens is filled with a clear, jelly-like substance called vitreous humour.
segments: Most of the space behind the lens is filled with a clear, jelly-like substance called vitreous humour.
cues.visualCue: Camera moves through vitreous toward the back

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: It helps maintain the shape of the eye.
segments: It helps maintain the shape of the eye.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: This inner layer at the back is the retina.
segments: This inner layer at the back is the retina.
cues.visualCue: Camera very close to retinal surface

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: It contains light-sensitive cells that detect light.
segments: It contains light-sensitive cells that detect light.
cues.visualCue: Retinal detail; camera moves slightly deeper

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Behind the retina is the choroid, a layer rich in blood vessels that supplies the eye with oxygen and nutrients.
segments: Behind the retina is the choroid, a layer rich in blood vessels that supplies the eye with oxygen and nutrients.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Now we’ve explored the main structures of the eye.
segments: Now we’ve explored the main structures of the eye.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: But there’s something important we haven’t explored yet.
segments: But there’s something important we haven’t explored yet.
cues.visualCue: Camera begins moving toward the back of the eye

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: We know that the retina detects light…
segments: We know that the retina detects light…
cues.visualCue: Back of the eye comes closer

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: …but how does that information reach the brain?
segments: …but how does that information reach the brain?

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Let’s follow it.
segments: Let’s follow it.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: This bundle is the optic nerve.
segments: This bundle is the optic nerve.
cues.visualCue: Close on optic nerve leaving the eye

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: It carries visual information from the retina to the brain.
segments: It carries visual information from the retina to the brain.
cues.visualCue: Camera follows nerve toward the brain

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: The brain receives and processes this information so that we can see.
segments: The brain receives and processes this information so that we can see.
cues.visualCue: Visual processing area at back of brain highlighted

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: So the eye and brain are connected through the optic nerve.
segments: So the eye and brain are connected through the optic nerve.
cues.visualCue: Wide: eye, optic nerve and brain together

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: We've been looking at the eye. Now let’s follow what happens when you look at an object.
segments: We've been looking at the eye. Now let’s follow what happens when you look at an object.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Vision begins when light from an object reaches the eye.
segments: Vision begins when light from an object reaches the eye.
cues.visualCue: Light travels from the object to the eye

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: First, the light passes through the cornea, which bends it.
segments: First, the light passes through the cornea, which bends it.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: It then travels through the aqueous humour and enters through the pupil.
segments: It then travels through the aqueous humour and enters through the pupil.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Change the brightness and observe what happens to the pupil.
segments: Change the brightness and observe what happens to the pupil.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: In bright light, the pupil becomes smaller.
segments: In bright light, the pupil becomes smaller.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: In dimmer light, the pupil becomes larger.
segments: In dimmer light, the pupil becomes larger.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: The iris controls the size of the pupil and therefore regulates how much light enters the eye.
segments: The iris controls the size of the pupil and therefore regulates how much light enters the eye.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: After passing through the pupil, the light reaches the eye’s crystalline lens.
segments: After passing through the pupil, the light reaches the eye’s crystalline lens.
cues.visualCue: Lens close-up; rays bend through lens

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: For a nearby object, the lens becomes more curved so that the light can be focused correctly.
segments: For a nearby object, the lens becomes more curved so that the light can be focused correctly.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: For a distant object, the lens becomes less curved.
segments: For a distant object, the lens becomes less curved.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: This continuous adjustment of the lens to focus objects at different distances is called accommodation.
segments: This continuous adjustment of the lens to focus objects at different distances is called accommodation.
cues.visualCue: Pull back: light continues through vitreous

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: After passing through the lens and vitreous humour, the light reaches the retina.
segments: After passing through the lens and vitreous humour, the light reaches the retina.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: The lens forms a real, inverted image of the object on the retina.
segments: The lens forms a real, inverted image of the object on the retina.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: But what exactly detects this light on the retina?
segments: But what exactly detects this light on the retina?

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: The retina contains light-sensitive cells called photoreceptors.
segments: The retina contains light-sensitive cells called photoreceptors.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Rods are especially sensitive to low levels of light and help us see in dim conditions.
segments: Rods are especially sensitive to low levels of light and help us see in dim conditions.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: They mainly provide information about brightness rather than colour.
segments: They mainly provide information about brightness rather than colour.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Cones work best in brighter light and allow us to see colours and fine details.
segments: Cones work best in brighter light and allow us to see colours and fine details.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: When light reaches these cells, it is converted into electrical signals.
segments: When light reaches these cells, it is converted into electrical signals.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: These signals are passed through the retina toward the optic nerve.
segments: These signals are passed through the retina toward the optic nerve.
cues.visualCue: Signals pass through retinal cells toward optic nerve

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: The electrical signals leave the eye through the optic nerve.
segments: The electrical signals leave the eye through the optic nerve.
cues.visualCue: Signals leave retina into optic nerve

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: The optic nerve carries this visual information to the brain.
segments: The optic nerve carries this visual information to the brain.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: The brain receives and processes these signals to produce our visual perception.
segments: The brain receives and processes these signals to produce our visual perception.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Although the image formed on the retina is inverted, our visual experience is not simply a photograph of that retinal image. The brain processes the information carried by the signals.
segments: Although the image formed on the retina is inverted, our visual experience is not simply a photograph of that retinal image.
The brain processes the information carried by the signals.
cues.visualCue: Original object shown clearly; retinal image and perception as separate views

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: So seeing is a complete process.
segments: So seeing is a complete process.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Now you’ve followed the journey from the moment light enters the eye to the moment the brain processes the information.
segments: Now you’ve followed the journey from the moment light enters the eye to the moment the brain processes the information.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Your eyes are constantly responding to the world around you—even when you’re not thinking about it.
segments: Your eyes are constantly responding to the world around you—even when you’re not thinking about it.

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: So here’s something to think about…what happens when the eye cannot focus light properly?
segments: So here’s something to think about…what happens when the eye cannot focus light properly?
cues.visualCue: Then distant object slightly blurred, near object clear

cues.speaker: Niko
cues.text: Why might some things look blurry, even when your eyes are working?
segments: Why might some things look blurry, even when your eyes are working?
cues.visualCue: Blurred object fades; eye fades; cut to black
